\section{Capped search and batch uniformity}\label{qua:app:capped-search}

We spell out the exact properties of the search primitive used in
\cref{qua:lem:capped-search}.  Start from the uniform superposition on $[M]$ and
use the randomized-iteration unknown-solution search of
Boyer--Brassard--Høyer--Tapp \cite{BBHT1998}.  If the marked density is at
least $\lambda$, truncate the geometric iteration schedule once its maximum
iteration count is a sufficiently large constant multiple of
$1/\sqrt\lambda$.  The standard analysis gives a success probability
$p_0>0$ independent of $M$ and $\lambda$, while the total number of
membership calls is $O(1/\sqrt\lambda)$.  The truncation is fixed before the
oracle outcomes are seen, so the block also terminates when there are no
marked states.

For any fixed Grover iteration count, the amplitudes of all marked basis
states are equal.  Mixing over the iteration count preserves this permutation
symmetry.  Measure the candidate and evaluate the exact membership predicate;
the block succeeds only when this verification accepts.  Conditional on
acceptance, every marked identity therefore has probability $1/|T|$.  A new
block reinitializes its registers and random choices, so accepted identities
from distinct blocks are independent conditional on the block-success
indicators.

For the batch statement, run
\[
 B=C\bigl(m+\log(1/\delta)\bigr)
\]
independent capped blocks, with $C$ an absolute constant chosen using $p_0$.
The number of accepted blocks stochastically dominates
$\operatorname{Bin}(B,p_0)$.  A Chernoff lower-tail bound makes the probability
of fewer than $m$ acceptances at most $\delta$.  Conditional on any success
pattern with at least $m$ acceptances, the first $m$ accepted identities are
independent and uniform on $T$.  This proves \cref{qua:lem:capped-search}.
